In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
ACh increases RBF and UV via the release of both PG and EDFR, and that L-arginine, the precursor of NO, is the only substrate for the synthesis of EDFR.
ACh stimulates both EDRF and PG release from the endothelial cells.
ACh stimulates the synthesis of both EDRF and PG, which in turn, mediate the renal vasodilation and diuresis, respectively, induced by ACh.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the ACh renal response is mediated by both EDRF and PG, but the participation of EDRF in mediating the ACh renal effect is greater than PG.
the ACh renal vasodilator effect is mainly mediated by EDRF and the diuretic effect by PG.
PG and EDRFs are the main mediators of the renal effects of acetylcholine, but the renal effects of PG and EDRFS are not additive.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ACh-mediated increases in RBF, UV, and UNaV are mediated by both EDRF and PG.
EDRF and PG have redundant functions in mediating the effects of ACh on RBF and UV.
ACh stimulates the renal vasodilation through a PG/EDRF-dependent mechanism.
